question: What is the primary duty of the trunk muscles compared to limb muscles?
explanation: Trunk muscles focus on encasing organs and stabilizing the central axis rather than executing limb movements. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why is the flexible connection provided by the trunk muscles important for the skeleton?

options.A: It locks the ribcage permanently in one position.
options.B: It prevents the spine from ever moving sideways.
options.C: It completely replaces the need for spinal vertebrae.
options.D: It allows bending and twisting without skeletal collapse.

explanation: The trunk muscles work with bones to create a strong yet mobile column for everyday body movements. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which abdominal muscle layer is the deepest and acts like a natural corset?
explanation: The transversus abdominis sits underneath the others, wrapping horizontally to compress the abdomen and support the spine. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h2)

question: How do the external and internal oblique muscles work together during movement?

options.A: They push the pelvic floor downward during heavy lifting.
options.B: They pull the spine straight backward to maintain an arched back.
options.C: Their crisscrossing fiber directions help the trunk rotate and twist safely.
options.D: They expand the ribcage independently to pull in extra oxygen.

explanation: The opposing angles of the oblique fibers allow smooth, controlled rotation of the torso. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is the main action when both sides of the erector spinae muscles contract together?
explanation: Bilateral contraction of the erector spinae straightens and extends the vertebral column. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h3)

question: Why is constant activity required from the deep back muscles even when standing still?

options.A: To fight the constant downward pull of gravity
options.B: To pump blood directly into the spinal cord
options.C: To prevent the hip joints from locking
options.D: To keep the lungs filled with resting air

explanation: Gravity constantly tries to pull the body forward and down, requiring continuous adjustments by postural back muscles. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h3)

question: What shape does the diaphragm take when it relaxes inside the body?
explanation: At rest, the diaphragm arches upward into a dome shape, then flattens out when it contracts during inhalation. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h4)

question: What physical change happens inside the chest cavity when the diaphragm contracts?

options.A: It stays the exact same size while ribs move.
options.B: It enlarges, causing air to rush into the lungs.
options.C: It shrinks completely, forcing all air outward.
options.D: It turns into solid bone to protect the heart.

explanation: Flattening the diaphragm increases thoracic volume, lowering pressure and drawing air inward. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT part of the deep core stability system?
explanation: The biceps brachii is an upper limb muscle, not part of the deep core stabilization cylinder. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h5)

question: Why do core muscles activate slightly BEFORE you lift a heavy object?

options.A: To relax the leg joints so bending is easier
options.B: To push blood out of the arms into the chest
options.C: To stabilize the spine and protect it from sudden injury
options.D: To warn the brain that the hands are opening

explanation: Anticipatory postural adjustment ensures the spine is braced before external loads place stress on the vertebrae. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h5)

question: Why might a patient with a painful abdominal surgical incision struggle with deep coughing?

options.A: Rib bones fuse together and block chest expansion.
options.B: Abdominal muscles cannot contract firmly to push air out.
options.C: The diaphragm stops receiving oxygen from the blood.
options.D: The lungs shrink in size permanently after any skin cut.

explanation: Coughing requires forceful contraction of the abdominal wall to generate pressure, which hurts when an incision is present. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h6)

question: A nurse is preparing to lift a heavy patient up in bed. How should the nurse protect their own trunk muscles?

options.A: Lean entirely backward while pulling the load.
options.B: Engage core stability and bend at the knees.
options.C: Use only arm strength without moving the feet.
options.D: Keep legs straight and twist quickly at the waist.

explanation: Bending the knees and bracing the core protects the spine from excessive shearing stress during heavy lifting tasks. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h6)
